title: Rate of Change: What the Ratio Actually Means

scenes.title: A tank drops from 90 L to 66 L in 6 minutes. What does the rate mean?
body: We want change in water per change in time.
scenes.narration: A tank has ninety liters at two minutes and sixty-six liters at eight minutes. What is its rate of change? Here’s the idea: rate of change tells us how much the output changes for each one unit of input. Here, the output is liters of water and the input is time.

scenes.title: Why we divide the two changes
scenes.narration: Why do we divide? Because the total change may happen over several input units. Dividing the output change by the input change converts that total change into a per-one-unit rate. That is exactly what slope means for a linear relationship: vertical change per horizontal change.

scenes.title: The common subtraction mistake
body: If you reverse one, reverse both.
scenes.narration: This is where students often mix things up. You can subtract either point first, but the order must match in the numerator and denominator. If you use sixty-six minus ninety for the water, you must use eight minus two for the time. Reversing only one subtraction flips the sign and changes the meaning.

scenes.title: Solve and interpret every step
scenes.narration: Now calculate. The water change is sixty-six minus ninety, which is negative twenty-four liters. The time change is eight minus two, which is six minutes. Negative twenty-four divided by six is negative four liters per minute. The negative sign is not an annoyance to drop; it tells us the amount of water is decreasing.

scenes.title: Check the meaning
body: Rate = output change per 1 input unit
scenes.equation: −4 L/min means lose 4 L each minute
scenes.narration: Quick check: losing four liters per minute for six minutes means losing twenty-four liters. Ninety minus twenty-four is sixty-six, exactly the second measurement. So the rate makes sense. Remember the idea: rate of change is output change per one input unit, so keep the subtraction order consistent and interpret the sign and units.
